     6	
     7	# Data Visualization Skill
     8	
     9	Chart selection guidance, Python visualization code patterns, design principles, and accessibility considerations for creating effective data visualizations.
    10	
    11	## Chart Selection Guide
    12	
    13	### Choose by Data Relationship
    14	
    15	| What You're Showing | Best Chart | Alternatives |
    16	|---|---|---|
    17	| **Trend over time** | Line chart | Area chart (if showing cumulative or composition) |
    18	| **Comparison across categories** | Vertical bar chart | Horizontal bar (many categories), lollipop chart |
    19	| **Ranking** | Horizontal bar chart | Dot plot, slope chart (comparing two periods) |
    20	| **Part-to-whole composition** | Stacked bar chart | Treemap (hierarchical), waffle chart |
    21	| **Composition over time** | Stacked area chart | 100% stacked bar (for proportion focus) |
    22	| **Distribution** | Histogram | Box plot (comparing groups), violin plot, strip plot |
    23	| **Correlation (2 variables)** | Scatter plot | Bubble chart (add 3rd variable as size) |
    24	| **Correlation (many variables)** | Heatmap (correlation matrix) | Pair plot |
    25	| **Geographic patterns** | Choropleth map | Bubble map, hex map |
    26	| **Flow / process** | Sankey diagram | Funnel chart (sequential stages) |
    27	| **Relationship network** | Network graph | Chord diagram |
    28	| **Performance vs. target** | Bullet chart | Gauge (single KPI only) |
    29	| **Multiple KPIs at once** | Small multiples | Dashboard with separate charts |
    30	
    31	### When NOT to Use Certain Charts
    32	
    33	- **Pie charts**: Avoid unless <6 categories and exact proportions matter less than rough comparison. Humans are bad at comparing angles. Use bar charts instead.
    34	- **3D charts**: Never. They distort perception and add no information.
    35	- **Dual-axis charts**: Use cautiously. They can mislead by implying correlation. Clearly label both axes if used.
    36	- **Stacked bar (many categories)**: Hard to compare middle segments. Use small multiples or grouped bars instead.
    37	- **Donut charts**: Slightly better than pie charts but same fundamental issues. Use for single KPI display at most.
    38	
    39	## Python Visualization Code Patterns
    40	
    41	### Setup and Style
    42	
    43	```python
    44	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    45	import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
    46	import seaborn as sns
    47	import pandas as pd
    48	import numpy as np
    49	
    50	# Professional style setup
    51	plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
    52	plt.rcParams.update({
    53	    'figure.figsize': (10, 6),
    54	    'figure.dpi': 150,
    55	    'font.size': 11,
    56	    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    57	    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    58	    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    59	    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    60	    'ytick.labelsize': 10,
    61	    'legend.fontsize': 10,
    62	    'figure.titlesize': 16,
    63	})
    64	
    65	# Colorblind-friendly palettes
    66	PALETTE_CATEGORICAL = ['#4C72B0', '#DD8452', '#55A868', '#C44E52', '#8172B3', '#937860']
    67	PALETTE_SEQUENTIAL = 'YlOrRd'
    68	PALETTE_DIVERGING = 'RdBu_r'
    69	```
    70	
    71	### Line Chart (Time Series)
    72	
    73	```python
    74	fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
    75	
    76	for label, group in df.groupby('category'):
    77	    ax.plot(group['date'], group['value'], label=label, linewidth=2)
    78	
    79	ax.set_title('Metric Trend by Category', fontweight='bold')
    80	ax.set_xlabel('Date')
    81	ax.set_ylabel('Value')
    82	ax.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True)
    83	ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    84	ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    85	
    86	# Format dates on x-axis
    87	fig.autofmt_xdate()
    88	
    89	plt.tight_layout()
    90	plt.savefig('trend_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
    91	```
    92	
    93	### Bar Chart (Comparison)
    94	
    95	```python
    96	fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
    97	
    98	# Sort by value for easy reading
    99	df_sorted = df.sort_values('metric', ascending=True)
   100	
   101	bars = ax.barh(df_sorted['category'], df_sorted['metric'], color=PALETTE_CATEGORICAL[0])
   102	
   103	# Add value labels
   104	for bar in bars:
   105	    width = bar.get_width()
   106	    ax.text(width + 0.5, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2,
   107	            f'{width:,.0f}', ha='left', va='center', fontsize=10)
   108	
   109	ax.set_title('Metric by Category (Ranked)', fontweight='bold')
   110	ax.set_xlabel('Metric Value')
   111	ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
   112	ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
   113	
   114	plt.tight_layout()
   115	plt.savefig('bar_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
   116	```
   117	
   118	### Histogram (Distribution)
   119	
   120	```python
   121	fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
   122	
   123	ax.hist(df['value'], bins=30, color=PALETTE_CATEGORICAL[0], edgecolor='white', alpha=0.8)
   124	
   125	# Add mean and median lines
   126	mean_val = df['value'].mean()
   127	median_val = df['value'].median()
   128	ax.axvline(mean_val, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, label=f'Mean: {mean_val:,.1f}')
   129	ax.axvline(median_val, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, label=f'Median: {median_val:,.1f}')
   130	
   131	ax.set_title('Distribution of Values', fontweight='bold')
   132	ax.set_xlabel('Value')
   133	ax.set_ylabel('Frequency')
   134	ax.legend()
   135	ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
   136	ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
   137	
   138	plt.tight_layout()
   139	plt.savefig('histogram.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
   140	```
   141	
   142	### Heatmap
   143	
   144	```python
   145	fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 8))
   146	
   147	# Pivot data for heatmap format
   148	pivot = df.pivot_table(index='row_dim', columns='col_dim', values='metric', aggfunc='sum')
   149	
   150	sns.heatmap(pivot, annot=True, fmt=',.0f', cmap='YlOrRd',
   151	            linewidths=0.5, ax=ax, cbar_kws={'label': 'Metric Value'})
   152	
   153	ax.set_title('Metric by Row Dimension and Column Dimension', fontweight='bold')
   154	ax.set_xlabel('Column Dimension')
   155	ax.set_ylabel('Row Dimension')
   156	
   157	plt.tight_layout()
   158	plt.savefig('heatmap.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
   159	```

   161	### Small Multiples
   162	
   163	```python
   164	categories = df['category'].unique()
   165	n_cats = len(categories)
   166	n_cols = min(3, n_cats)
   167	n_rows = (n_cats + n_cols - 1) // n_cols
   168	
   169	fig, axes = plt.subplots(n_rows, n_cols, figsize=(5*n_cols, 4*n_rows), sharex=True, sharey=True)
   170	axes = axes.flatten() if n_cats > 1 else [axes]
   171	
   172	for i, cat in enumerate(categories):
   173	    ax = axes[i]
   174	    subset = df[df['category'] == cat]
   175	    ax.plot(subset['date'], subset['value'], color=PALETTE_CATEGORICAL[i % len(PALETTE_CATEGORICAL)])
   176	    ax.set_title(cat, fontsize=12)
   177	    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
   178	    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
   179	
   180	# Hide empty subplots
   181	for j in range(i+1, len(axes)):
   182	    axes[j].set_visible(False)
   183	
   184	fig.suptitle('Trends by Category', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
   185	plt.tight_layout()
   186	plt.savefig('small_multiples.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
   187	```

   189	### Number Formatting Helpers
   190	
   191	```python
   192	def format_number(val, format_type='number'):
   193	    """Format numbers for chart labels."""
   194	    if format_type == 'currency':
   195	        if abs(val) >= 1e9:
   196	            return f'${val/1e9:.1f}B'
   197	        elif abs(val) >= 1e6:
   198	            return f'${val/1e6:.1f}M'
   199	        elif abs(val) >= 1e3:
   200	            return f'${val/1e3:.1f}K'
   201	        else:
   202	            return f'${val:,.0f}'
   203	    elif format_type == 'percent':
   204	        return f'{val:.1f}%'
   205	    elif format_type == 'number':
   206	        if abs(val) >= 1e9:
   207	            return f'{val/1e9:.1f}B'
   208	        elif abs(val) >= 1e6:
   209	            return f'{val/1e6:.1f}M'
   210	        elif abs(val) >= 1e3:
   211	            return f'{val/1e3:.1f}K'
   212	        else:
   213	            return f'{val:,.0f}'
   214	    return str(val)
   215	
   216	# Usage with axis formatter
   217	ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: format_number(x, 'currency')))
   218	```

   220	### Interactive Charts with Plotly
   221	
   222	```python
   223	import plotly.express as px
   224	import plotly.graph_objects as go
   225	
   226	# Simple interactive line chart
   227	fig = px.line(df, x='date', y='value', color='category',
   228	              title='Interactive Metric Trend',
   229	              labels={'value': 'Metric Value', 'date': 'Date'})
   230	fig.update_layout(hovermode='x unified')
   231	fig.write_html('interactive_chart.html')
   232	fig.show()
   233	
   234	# Interactive scatter with hover data
   235	fig = px.scatter(df, x='metric_a', y='metric_b', color='category',
   236	                 size='size_metric', hover_data=['name', 'detail_field'],
   237	                 title='Correlation Analysis')
   238	fig.show()
   239	```

   241	## Design Principles
   242	
   243	### Color
   244	
   245	- **Use color purposefully**: Color should encode data, not decorate
   246	- **Highlight the story**: Use a bright accent color for the key insight; grey everything else
   247	- **Sequential data**: Use a single-hue gradient (light to dark) for ordered values
   248	- **Diverging data**: Use a two-hue gradient with neutral midpoint for data with a meaningful center
   249	- **Categorical data**: Use distinct hues, maximum 6-8 before it gets confusing
   250	- **Avoid red/green only**: 8% of men are red-green colorblind. Use blue/orange as primary pair
   251	
   252	### Typography
   253	
   254	- **Title states the insight**: "Revenue grew 23% YoY" beats "Revenue by Month"
   255	- **Subtitle adds context**: Date range, filters applied, data source
   256	- **Axis labels are readable**: Never rotated 90 degrees if avoidable. Shorten or wrap instead
   257	- **Data labels add precision**: Use on key points, not every single bar
   258	- **Annotation highlights**: Call out specific points with text annotations
   259	
   260	### Layout
   261	
   262	- **Reduce chart junk**: Remove gridlines, borders, backgrounds that don't carry information
   263	- **Sort meaningfully**: Categories sorted by value (not alphabetically) unless there's a natural order (months, stages)
   264	- **Appropriate aspect ratio**: Time series wider than tall (3:1 to 2:1); comparisons can be squarer
   265	- **White space is good**: Don't cram charts together. Give each visualization room to breathe
   266	
   267	### Accuracy
   268	
   269	- **Bar charts start at zero**: Always. A bar from 95 to 100 exaggerates a 5% difference
   270	- **Line charts can have non-zero baselines**: When the range of variation is meaningful
   271	- **Consistent scales across panels**: When comparing multiple charts, use the same axis range
   272	- **Show uncertainty**: Error bars, confidence intervals, or ranges when data is uncertain
   273	- **Label your axes**: Never make the reader guess what the numbers mean
   274	
   275	## Accessibility Considerations
   276	
   277	### Color Blindness
   278	
   279	- Never rely on color alone to distinguish data series
   280	- Add pattern fills, different line styles (solid, dashed, dotted), or direct labels
   281	- Test with a colorblind simulator (e.g., Coblis, Sim Daltonism)
   282	- Use the colorblind-friendly palette: `sns.color_palette("colorblind")`
   283	
   284	### Screen Readers
   285	
   286	- Include alt text describing the chart's key finding
   287	- Provide a data table alternative alongside the visualization
   288	- Use semantic titles and labels
   289	
   290	### General Accessibility
   291	
   292	- Sufficient contrast between data elements and background
   293	- Text size minimum 10pt for labels, 12pt for titles
   294	- Avoid conveying information only through spatial position (add labels)
   295	- Consider printing: does the chart work in black and white?
   296	
   297	### Accessibility Checklist
   298	
   299	Before sharing a visualization:
   300	- [ ] Chart works without color (patterns, labels, or line styles differentiate series)
   301	- [ ] Text is readable at standard zoom level
   302	- [ ] Title describes the insight, not just the data
   303	- [ ] Axes are labeled with units
   304	- [ ] Legend is clear and positioned without obscuring data
   305	- [ ] Data source and date range are noted

1	# Kubernetes Multi-Environment Deployment Pipeline
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	This dataset describes a Kubernetes deployment pipeline spanning four environments (dev, staging, canary, production) with automated rollback mechanisms, blue-green traffic switching at the production stage, and HPA (Horizontal Pod Autoscaler) scaling decision points at every environment.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### pipeline_nodes
     9	34 nodes representing pipeline steps. Fields: `id` (string, unique identifier), `label` (string, human-readable name), `lane` (string: dev | staging | canary | production | global), `type` (string: action | check | decision | hpa_decision | hpa_action | rollback | terminal), `order` (integer, sequencing hint). Some nodes carry additional threshold fields such as `cpu_threshold_pct`, `mem_threshold_pct`, `error_rate_threshold_pct`, `p99_latency_ms_threshold`, `traffic_pct`, and `duration_min`.
    10	
    11	### pipeline_edges
    12	48 directed edges. Fields: `from` and `to` (node id references), `type` (string: forward | rollback | hpa_branch | blue_green), `label` (string, condition or annotation on the edge).
    13	
    14	### hpa_policies
    15	4 rows, one per environment. Fields: `environment`, `min_replicas`, `max_replicas`, `cpu_target_pct`, `mem_target_pct`, `scale_up_cooldown_sec`, `scale_down_cooldown_sec`. Replica counts are integers; thresholds are percentages.
    16	
    17	### environment_config
    18	4 rows. Fields: `environment`, `namespace`, `gate_error_rate_pct` (float), `gate_p99_latency_ms` (integer or null), `traffic_strategy` (string: direct | weighted_canary | blue_green), `rollback_auto` (boolean), `approval_required` (boolean).
    19	
    20	## Data Notes
    21	- Threshold values tighten progressively from dev to production (e.g., error-rate gate: 5% → 2% → 1% → 0.5%).
    22	- The canary stage uses three progressive traffic ramp steps (10% → 25% → 50%) before the production gate.
    23	- Blue-green switching applies only to the production environment; other environments use direct or weighted-canary strategies.
    24	- HPA scale-up and scale-down nodes are shared (global lane) and referenced from each environment's HPA check.

import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch, FancyArrowPatch
import numpy as np

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

nodes = {n['id']: n for n in data['pipeline_nodes']['data']}
edges = data['pipeline_edges']['data']
hpa_policies = {p['environment']: p for p in data['hpa_policies']['data']}
env_config = {c['environment']: c for c in data['environment_config']['data']}

# Setup style - data-dense, technical, team-internal
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams.update({
    'figure.figsize': (28, 20),
    'figure.dpi': 150,
    'font.size': 9,
    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 10,
    'xtick.labelsize': 9,
    'ytick.labelsize': 9,
    'legend.fontsize': 9,
    'figure.titlesize': 16,
})

# Color scheme - professional, colorblind-friendly, technical
LANE_COLORS = {
    'dev': '#E8F4FD',
    'staging': '#E6F5E6',
    'canary': '#FFF8E1',
    'production': '#F3E5F5',
    'global': '#F5F5F5',
}

LANE_LABEL_COLORS = {
    'dev': '#1565C0',
    'staging': '#2E7D32',
    'canary': '#F57F17',
    'production': '#6A1B9A',
    'global': '#424242',
}

NODE_COLORS = {
    'action': '#4C72B0',
    'check': '#55A868',
    'decision': '#DD8452',
    'hpa_decision': '#8172B3',
    'hpa_action': '#937860',
    'rollback': '#C44E52',
    'terminal': '#2E7D32',
}

EDGE_COLORS = {
    'forward': '#333333',
    'rollback': '#C44E52',
    'hpa_branch': '#8172B3',
    'blue_green': '#6A1B9A',
}

# Layout: swimlanes stacked vertically
LANE_ORDER = ['dev', 'staging', 'canary', 'production', 'global']
LANE_HEIGHT = 2.8
LANE_GAP = 0.3
NODE_WIDTH = 2.2
NODE_HEIGHT = 0.7

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(28, 20))
ax.set_xlim(-1, 32)
ax.set_ylim(-1, 17)
ax.axis('off')

# Title and subtitle
fig.suptitle('Kubernetes Multi-Environment Deployment Pipeline', 
             fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)
ax.text(15.5, 16.3, 
        'End-to-end flow: Dev → Staging → Canary → Production  |  Rollbacks, HPA Scaling & Blue-Green Switching',
        ha='center', va='center', fontsize=11, style='italic', color='#555555')

# Draw swimlane backgrounds and labels
lane_y_positions = {}
for i, lane in enumerate(LANE_ORDER):
    y_bottom = 15.5 - i * (LANE_HEIGHT + LANE_GAP)
    lane_y_positions[lane] = y_bottom
    
    # Background
    rect = FancyBboxPatch((-0.5, y_bottom - LANE_HEIGHT/2 - 0.1), 32, LANE_HEIGHT + 0.2,
                           boxstyle="round,pad=0.05", 
                           facecolor=LANE_COLORS[lane], edgecolor=LANE_LABEL_COLORS[lane],
                           linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.4, zorder=0)
    ax.add_patch(rect)
    
    # Lane label
    ax.text(-0.3, y_bottom, lane.upper(), ha='left', va='center', 
            fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', color=LANE_LABEL_COLORS[lane],
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white', 
                     edgecolor=LANE_LABEL_COLORS[lane], linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.9))

# Position nodes within lanes
node_positions = {}
# Distribute nodes horizontally within each lane by order
lane_nodes = {lane: [] for lane in LANE_ORDER}
for nid, node in nodes.items():
    lane = node['lane']
    if lane in lane_nodes:
        lane_nodes[lane].append(node)

for lane in LANE_ORDER:
    items = sorted(lane_nodes[lane], key=lambda x: x['order'])
    n_items = len(items)
    if n_items == 0:
        continue
    # Spread across x from 2 to 30
    xs = np.linspace(2.5, 29, n_items) if n_items > 1 else [15]
    y_base = lane_y_positions[lane]
    for i, node in enumerate(items):
        node_positions[node['id']] = (xs[i], y_base)

# Helper: draw node
def draw_node(ax, nid, x, y):
    node = nodes[nid]
    ntype = node['type']
    color = NODE_COLORS.get(ntype, '#888888')
    label = node['label']
    
    # Shape based on type
    if ntype == 'decision':
        shape = 'diamond'
        w, h = NODE_WIDTH * 0.9, NODE_HEIGHT * 1.3
    elif ntype == 'terminal':
        shape = 'round'
        w, h = NODE_WIDTH * 1.1, NODE_HEIGHT
    elif ntype == 'rollback':
        shape = 'round'
        w, h = NODE_WIDTH * 1.0, NODE_HEIGHT
    else:
        shape = 'round'
        w, h = NODE_WIDTH, NODE_HEIGHT
    
    if shape == 'diamond':
        diamond = plt.Polygon([(x, y+h/2), (x+w/2, y), (x, y-h/2), (x-w/2, y)],
                              facecolor=color, edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.2, zorder=3, alpha=0.9)
        ax.add_patch(diamond)
    else:
        rect = FancyBboxPatch((x - w/2, y - h/2), w, h,
                              boxstyle="round,pad=0.05,rounding_size=0.15",
                              facecolor=color, edgecolor='black', linewidth=1.2, zorder=3, alpha=0.9)
        ax.add_patch(rect)
    
    # Text
    ax.text(x, y, label, ha='center', va='center', fontsize=7.5,
            fontweight='bold', color='white', zorder=4, wrap=True)
    
    return (x, y, w, h)

# Helper: draw edge with arrow
def draw_edge(ax, x1, y1, x2, y2, etype, label='', curvature=0):
    color = EDGE_COLORS.get(etype, '#888888')
    lw = 2 if etype == 'forward' else 1.8
    style = '-' if etype == 'forward' else '--'
    
    # For rollback edges, use dashed red
    if etype == 'rollback':
        style = '--'
    elif etype == 'hpa_branch':
        style = '-.'
    elif etype == 'blue_green':
        style = '-'
        lw = 2.5
    
    # Calculate control point for curvature
    if curvature != 0:
        mid_x = (x1 + x2) / 2
        mid_y = (y1 + y2) / 2
        # Perpendicular offset
        dx = x2 - x1
        dy = y2 - y1
        length = np.sqrt(dx**2 + dy**2)
        if length > 0:
            perp_x = -dy / length * curvature
            perp_y = dx / length * curvature
            ctrl_x = mid_x + perp_x
            ctrl_y = mid_y + perp_y
            
            t = np.linspace(0, 1, 50)
            # Quadratic Bezier
            bx = (1-t)**2 * x1 + 2*(1-t)*t * ctrl_x + t**2 * x2
            by = (1-t)**2 * y1 + 2*(1-t)*t * ctrl_y + t**2 * y2
            ax.plot(bx, by, color=color, linewidth=lw, linestyle=style, zorder=1, alpha=0.85)
            
            # Arrow at end
            arrow_idx = -3
            ax.annotate('', xy=(bx[arrow_idx+1], by[arrow_idx+1]),
                       xytext=(bx[arrow_idx], by[arrow_idx]),
                       arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color, lw=lw),
                       zorder=2)
        else:
            ax.plot([x1, x2], [y1, y2], color=color, linewidth=lw, linestyle=style, zorder=1, alpha=0.85)
    else:
        ax.annotate('', xy=(x2, y2), xytext=(x1, y1),
                   arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=color, lw=lw, 
                                  linestyle=style, connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0'),
                   zorder=2)
    
    # Edge label
    if label:
        mid_x = (x1 + x2) / 2
        mid_y = (y1 + y2) / 2
        if curvature != 0:
            dx = x2 - x1
            dy = y2 - y1
            length = np.sqrt(dx**2 + dy**2)
            if length > 0:
                perp_x = -dy / length * curvature
                perp_y = dx / length * curvature
                mid_x += perp_x * 0.5
                mid_y += perp_y * 0.5
        
        # Offset label slightly
        offset_y = 0.25 if y2 >= y1 else -0.25
        ax.text(mid_x, mid_y + offset_y, label, ha='center', va='bottom' if y2 >= y1 else 'top',
               fontsize=6.5, color=color, fontweight='bold', 
               bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.15', facecolor='white', edgecolor='none', alpha=0.8),
               zorder=5)

# Draw all nodes first (to get positions)
node_bboxes = {}
for nid, (x, y) in node_positions.items():
    node_bboxes[nid] = draw_node(ax, nid, x, y)

# Draw edges
# To avoid overlapping too much, track which edges need curvature
edge_counts = {}
for edge in edges:
    key = tuple(sorted([edge['from'], edge['to']]))
    edge_counts[key] = edge_counts.get(key, 0) + 1

# Pre-calculate edge curvatures
edge_curvature = {}
for edge in edges:
    key = tuple(sorted([edge['from'], edge['to']]))
    if edge_counts[key] > 1:
        # Need curvature for duplicate edges
        if key not in edge_curvature:
            edge_curvature[key] = []
        edge_curvature[key].append(edge)

# Draw edges
for edge in edges:
    f, t = edge['from'], edge['to']
    if f not in node_positions or t not in node_positions:
        continue
    x1, y1 = node_positions[f]
    x2, y2 = node_positions[t]
    
    # Adjust to node boundary
    def boundary_point(px, py, qx, qy, w, h):
        dx = qx - px
        dy = qy - py
        if abs(dx) < 0.01 and abs(dy) < 0.01:
            return px, py
        # Simplified: use direction to edge of rectangle
        ratio = min(w/2 / abs(dx) if dx != 0 else float('inf'),
                   h/2 / abs(dy) if dy != 0 else float('inf'))
        ratio = min(ratio, 1.0)
        return px + dx * ratio * 0.9, py + dy * ratio * 0.9
    
    _, _, w1, h1 = node_bboxes[f]
    _, _, w2, h2 = node_bboxes[t]
    bx1, by1 = boundary_point(x1, y1, x2, y2, w1, h1)
    bx2, by2 = boundary_point(x2, y2, x1, y1, w2, h2)
    
    # Determine curvature
    key = tuple(sorted([f, t]))
    curvature = 0
    if edge_counts[key] > 1:
        idx = edge_curvature[key].index(edge)
        # Alternate curvature direction
        curvature = 0.4 * (1 if idx % 2 == 0 else -0.4)
        # For same node pair, use stronger curve
        curvature = 0.6 * (1 if idx % 2 == 0 else -1)
    
    # Special handling for cross-lane edges
    lane1 = nodes[f]['lane']
    lane2 = nodes[t]['lane']
    if lane1 != lane2 and edge['type'] == 'rollback':
        # Rollback to global lane
        if lane2 == 'global':
            curvature = -0.5
        elif lane1 == 'global':
            curvature = 0.5
    
    # HPA branch edges - curve outward
    if edge['type'] == 'hpa_branch':
        curvature = 0.5 if 'scale-up' in t else -0.5
    
    draw_edge(ax, bx1, by1, bx2, by2, edge['type'], edge['label'], curvature)

# Legend for node types
legend_elements = [
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=NODE_COLORS['action'], edgecolor='black', label='Action'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=NODE_COLORS['check'], edgecolor='black', label='Health/Check'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=NODE_COLORS['decision'], edgecolor='black', label='Decision Gate'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=NODE_COLORS['hpa_decision'], edgecolor='black', label='HPA Check'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=NODE_COLORS['hpa_action'], edgecolor='black', label='HPA Action'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=NODE_COLORS['rollback'], edgecolor='black', label='Rollback'),
    mpatches.Patch(facecolor=NODE_COLORS['terminal'], edgecolor='black', label='Complete'),
]
legend1 = ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper right', 
                   bbox_to_anchor=(0.99, 0.99), title='Node Types', 
                   title_fontsize=10, fontsize=8, frameon=True, fancybox=True)
ax.add_artist(legend1)

# Legend for edge types
edge_legend = [
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], color=EDGE_COLORS['forward'], linewidth=2, label='Forward Flow'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], color=EDGE_COLORS['rollback'], linewidth=2, linestyle='--', label='Rollback'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], color=EDGE_COLORS['hpa_branch'], linewidth=2, linestyle='-.', label='HPA Branch'),
    plt.Line2D([0], [0], color=EDGE_COLORS['blue_green'], linewidth=2.5, label='Blue-Green'),
]
ax.legend(handles=edge_legend, loc='upper right',
         bbox_to_anchor=(0.99, 0.88), title='Edge Types',
         title_fontsize=10, fontsize=8, frameon=True, fancybox=True)

# HPA threshold annotation box
hpa_text = "HPA Thresholds:\n"
for env in ['dev', 'staging', 'canary', 'production']:
    p = hpa_policies[env]
    hpa_text += f"• {env.capitalize()}: CPU {p['cpu_target_pct']}%, Mem {p['mem_target_pct']}% | Replicas {p['min_replicas']}-{p['max_replicas']}\n"

ax.text(0.01, 0.01, hpa_text, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7.5,
       verticalalignment='bottom', horizontalalignment='left',
       bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='#FAFAFA', edgecolor='#CCCCCC', alpha=0.95))

# Gate thresholds annotation
gate_text = "Gate Thresholds:\n"
for env in ['dev', 'staging', 'canary', 'production']:
    c = env_config[env]
    lat = f", p99<{c['gate_p99_latency_ms']}ms" if c['gate_p99_latency_ms'] else ""
    gate_text += f"• {env.capitalize()}: Error<{c['gate_error_rate_pct']}% {lat}\n"

ax.text(0.35, 0.01, gate_text, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=7.5,
       verticalalignment='bottom', horizontalalignment='left',
       bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='#FAFAFA', edgecolor='#CCCCCC', alpha=0.95))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
plt.close()
print("Chart saved to /app/output/result.png")
